title: 2023 AMC 12B Problem 8
statement: How many nonempty subsets \(B\) of \(\{0,1,2,3,\ldots,12\}\) have the property that the number of elements in \(B\) is equal to the least element of \(B?\) For example, \(B=\{4,6,8,11\}\) satisfies the condition.

solutions.text:
If the least element is \(m\ (m\ge 1),\) then \(|B|=m\) and the remaining \(m-1\) elements come from \(\{m+1,\ldots,12\},\) a set of size \(12-m.\) The count is \[ \begin{aligned} \sum_{m\ge 1}\binom{12-m}{m-1} &=\binom{11}{0} \\ &\quad {}+\binom{10}{1} \\ &\quad {}+\binom{9}{2} \\ &\quad {}+\binom{8}{3} \\ &\quad {}+\binom{7}{4} \\ &\quad {}+\binom{6}{5}, \end{aligned} \] which equals \(1+10+36+56+35+6\) \(=144.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: If the least element is \(m,\) then \(B\) has exactly \(m\) elements, all at least \(m\)
Choose the other \(m-1\) elements from the \(12-m\) integers greater than \(m:\) this gives \(\binom{12-m}{m-1}\)
